This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via unrecognized_keys (literal, a string literal in valueShapeDetail))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via unrecognized_keys (literal, a string literal in valueShapeDetail))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `faffb3fa01a71ae74c1f41e869f71cfa0e6eae17` — the merge of head `55cf89916e46ef675a9ce842d9740bb38fa076cb` into base `51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin faffb3fa01a71ae74c1f41e869f71cfa0e6eae17 && git checkout faffb3fa01a71ae74c1f41e869f71cfa0e6eae17
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501 55cf89916e46ef675a9ce842d9740bb38fa076cb && git checkout -B drift-repro 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501 && git merge --no-ff 55cf89916e46ef675a9ce842d9740bb38fa076cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `55cf89916e46ef675a9ce842d9740bb38fa076cb`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22908 (body, triage grade 6115825886, claim 6116778532, os-dev-report 6117876326), PR #22947 (body, its one bot comment, 4-file list, 4 commits), the net diff of the branch against `origin/main` from merge base `018b077fbf` (490 additions / 31 deletions; `record-validator.ts` is the only source change, plus two tests and one changeset), the check-runs on the head, and on `origin/main` the files the brief names, read to judge what changes. PR #22907's `reference-shape.test.ts` read as the instrument's cited context. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What changes.** `validateOne`'s multi-value branch no longer returns `null` for `lookup` / `user` / `file` / `image`. The branch is gated on `!isValueShapeJudgedType(t)` and judges option types only; the four value-shape types fall through to the ADR-0104 D1 arm, which parses the whole value with `shapeSchemaFor(def)`, that is `valueSchemaFor(def, 'stored')`, which is already `z.array(element)` for a field `isMultiValueField` accepts (`MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` is select, radio, lookup, user, file, image). The element rule is therefore the single value's own: `ReferenceIdValueSchema` for `lookup` / `user` (a non-empty string that is not embedded-record JSON text), `FileReferenceIdValueSchema` for `file` / `image` (an opaque `sys_file` id, bounded charset). One shape rule kept, no second rule written anywhere in the diff. Right.

2. **Which writes are refused, under which posture.** Posture is unchanged and shared with the single value. References: `valueShapeStrictEffective(valueStrict)`, where `OS_ALLOW_LAX_VALUE_SHAPES=1` (opt-out) beats `OS_DATA_VALUE_SHAPE_STRICT_ENABLED=1` (all-class opt-in) beats the deployment's verified `adr-0104-value-shapes` row (a born-attested fresh store, or `os migrate value-shapes --apply`), consulted only when the object declares a scannable covered field (`objectHasCoveredValueField` via `isScannableValueShapeField`, the dormancy rule). Media: `mediaStrictEffective(mediaStrict)` with `OS_ALLOW_LAX_MEDIA_VALUES` and the `adr-0104-file-references` row, dormant unless the object declares a media field. Under strict, an embedded record, a boolean or a number as an element of a `lookup` / `user` with `multiple: true` is refused `invalid_type`. Right. The same rule also refuses any other non-id element (`null`, an empty or whitespace string): that goes past the card's three named shapes but is the single value's `z.string().min(1)`, the scan already counted exactly these at base, and the changeset's TO states the rule rather than only the three examples. Right, and named here because a single-valued blank is `isMissing` and never reaches the arm while a blank element inside an array does; `multiValueStorageForm` does not wrap blanks and `normalizeBlankTypedValues` leaves string-stored columns alone, so nothing upstream removes one. Inherent in the shared schema, not a defect. Under warn-first the element is admitted, `warnOnce`-logged and reported to `onAdmittedValueShapeViolation` with gate `value-shape` or `media`, the field, the type and the index-bearing detail. Right, pinned.

3. **Both doors.** The check is `validateRecord` / `validateRecordInScope`'s, which the engine runs on insert (single and batch) and on both update passes for every context, so the caller's door (the engine call the REST data routes make) and the system write (`isSystem`) refuse alike under strict. Pinned at engine level for caller and system contexts, insert and update, with the row count and the held value unchanged after the refusal. `assertReferencesResolve` is not in the diff: its early return for `context.isSystem` and its skip of an object-typed element stand, so #4551's existence latitude is untouched. Right, pinned by the engine test's last case (a well-formed id naming no row is `reference_not_found` for the caller and still stored by the system principal). Under warn-first a caller's boolean or number element still meets the existence check and answers `reference_not_found` as before.

4. **`file` / `image` with `multiple: true`.** Each element is held to `FileReferenceIdValueSchema` under the media posture; a verified media flag does not open reference elements and the value-shape flag does not open media elements. Pinned with the two flags crossed. `avatar` / `video` / `audio` are not multi-capable, so unreached. Right.

5. **Scan predicate and write path.** `valueShapeViolation` now uses `isValueShapeJudgedType` and the `def`-aware `valueShapeDetail`; `scanValueShapes` imports it unchanged; the validator test pins scan-equals-strict-write on six probes per field. At base the scan already walked the `z.array` form while the write path admitted the element; that disagreement, which contradicted the scan's own header, is closed. `isScannableValueShapeField` (which fields are walked: references and structured JSON, never system or readonly, never media) is unchanged. Right.

6. **Readonly multi-valued references.** Before, `if (shapeOnly) return null;` left the branch ahead of any element check; now the four types bypass that gate and reach the arm, which the single readonly value already reached under the #21663 ruling. So a readonly multi-valued `lookup` / `user` / `file` / `image` written by a system writer, hook or stamp is shape-judged under the object's posture (pinned, `stamped_team`). Right, the ruling applied to the other cardinality; named because a platform writer storing an off-shape element in such a column on a born-strict store is now refused at that write. The Test Core and Dogfood shards on this head are the canary (see the pending runs in ③).

7. **Error envelope.** `ValidationError`, code `VALIDATION_FAILED` (the pre-existing REST mapping answers 400, which the dev's real-door reading reports), one `fields[]` entry `{ field, code: 'invalid_type', constraint: { type, detail } }`, message key `invalid_value_shape`, whose template renders the detail. The index is carried as text: `at index N:` prefixed to the chosen zod issue's message from its `path[0]`, only when `isMultiValueField(def)`; the single value's detail is unchanged (pinned: no index named on the controls), and `repeater` / `vector` are not `isMultiValueField`, so unprefixed. The wrong element at position 2 is named as index 2 (pinned). Triage asked for the field and the index to be named; they are. No structured index key is added, which is consistent with how the scan's `ValueShapeFinding.detail` already carries the prescription. Right.

8. **Exports and public surface.** `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` is untouched; `isValueShapeJudgedType` is module-private; the private `valueShapeDetail` gains a `def` parameter; the exported `valueShapeViolation` signature is unchanged; no spec change, no new key, no new env var, no wire-shape change. "No export change" is right.

9. **Option types.** For multiselect `select` / `radio` and the multi-option types the branch behaves as before (`shapeOnly` gate, `picklistUnresolved`, `invalid_option` with kept options). Right.

10. **Claim surface honoured.** The diff is exactly `record-validator.ts`, two tests beside the code (`src/validation/` for the validator, `src/` beside `engine.ts` for the engine door), one changeset; `engine.ts` read-only. Merge base matches the claim's read sha; the dev's line budget (490 / 31 over 4 files) matches the PR.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/22908-multi-reference-element-shape.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` at `minor`, the only package the diff publishes; a BREAKING banner naming it an accept-set narrowing, shipped `minor` under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major` records; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its argument (no spec key, authorable spelling, export or stored shape moves; stored rows are `os migrate value-shapes` / `files-to-references` business); FROM / TO stated per door and per posture; the one-line fix stated (write ids as elements, never the record a read with expand returns). Level and marker match what the diff publishes. Right. `Check Changeset` is green on the head; `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` ride `Lint & Repo Gates`, still in progress at the final read (the dev reports both at exit 0 on this head).
- **Agreement of the `Clause-②:` line.** PR body line 2, the changeset body, the claim and triage's grade all read `yes (narrowing)`. They agree.
- **Is `yes (narrowing)` legal here?** It is a legal spelling: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the fleet's one reader, accepts four combinations and refuses only `no (widening)`; AGENTS.md says the same. It is not the accurate value. The value answers one question, whether the card widens a published accept set or the public surface, and this diff widens nothing (①.8): it only narrows. The reader's own gloss reserves `yes (narrowing)` for a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; the dispatch's rule text says a card that only narrows is `Clause-②: no`; the lane's two precedents (#22519, #22856) carry `no (narrowing)` for the same class. The dev flagged it and did not re-rule, which is right: the value is triage's and the claim's. Consequence for the gates: none. The `yes` floor (at least `minor`) is met by the `minor` a BREAKING narrowing takes anyway, and the ADR-0087 disposition is demanded by the `narrowing` arm and the banner, which both gates read identically under either value; the mis-declaration errs toward more review, not less. **Correction owed by the seat, not by a respin:** `no (narrowing)` on the claim and on the PR body line 2 (a body edit); the changeset's own line follows the next time the head moves. Not a reason to withhold PASS.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every `deviations` entry and every `out_of_scope_findings` entry of os-dev-report 6117876326 is answered below; `open_questions` is empty.

- **D1, the Clause-② arm.** Answered in ②: legal spelling, inaccurate value, no gate consequence, seat correction owed.
- **D2, the real-door pin one-off rather than kept.** Verified on `origin/main`: the `@objectstack/verify` real-stack fixture in `reference-shape.test.ts` (`rs_contact`) declares single-valued reference fields only; the `multiple: true` `rs_board.accounts` sits in the derivation test alone. So no in-tree test drives PR #22907's family over a multi-valued field on a real stack, and the dev's one-off (48 of 48 refused on the fixed build; 16 admitted under ablation, reproducing the card's measurement) is evidence read from the report, not a pin. Accepted here: the claim's file surface is tests beside the code, and the kept engine pin drives both contexts through the same engine door the REST data routes call. **Escalated to the seat:** the card for the separate `os verify --reference-shapes` default call (triage's not-folded item, #22907's recommendation) carries, in its scope, a `multiple: true` `lookup` and `user` in the verify real-stack fixture so the family's multi-valued rows become permanent. Not blocking.
- **D3, ablation attempt 1 a no-op.** The tool refused before running and restored the HEAD blob; the second attempt's reading (43 pins failed, the 10 controls passed; restore verified blob-equal, tree clean, 53 of 53 after) is the one that counts. Procedural, answered.
- **D4, attribution.** The four commits carry the AGENTS.md pair, `Co-authored-by: Claude` and a `Claude-Session` trailer naming the dispatching session; AGENTS.md's attribution rule is the one that binds over a harness reminder. Right.
- **D5, gates re-run at the final head.** Every figure reported is from the head under review; CI on the same head agrees so far (28 success, 0 failure). Answered.
- **O1, the scan already reports stored multi-valued elements.** Verified from source: `valueShapeViolation` went through `shapeSchemaFor` (the `z.array` form) at base and `isScannableValueShapeField` does not exclude `multiple`, so the triage's conditional gap card is not owed. Right.
- **O2, the authoring-time default-value gate names no index.** A separate reading in `packages/spec` by design; polish, outside the filing classes; carrier none. Agreed.
- **O3, the objectui console write path, NOT MEASURED.** Answered as far as this repository answers it, then escalated.
  - The showcase declares `project.team_members` (`Field.user`, `multiple: true`) and `project.view.ts` renders it as a list column and a form field; no in-repo seed, dogfood script or verify fixture writes it, so a console save is its only producer and no check on this head exercises it.
  - A warn-first deployment (an existing store with no verified `adr-0104-value-shapes` row and no env switch, which is what an upgraded store is) refuses nothing a console save sends that it did not refuse before: a wrong element is admitted, logged and tallied; a boolean or number element still meets the caller's existence check and answers `reference_not_found` as before.
  - A strict deployment refuses a console save whose multi-valued `lookup` / `user` element is not a non-empty id string (an expanded record object, a boolean, a number, `null`, an empty string) and whose multi-valued `file` / `image` element is not a `sys_file` id (a URL string, an expanded file object). Strict is wider than the brief's framing of the default: per ADR-0104 every fresh store is born-attested, so every showcase or CRM fresh boot and every dogfood run is strict from birth, as is a store after the scan's `--apply` or under `OS_DATA_VALUE_SHAPE_STRICT_ENABLED=1`. Under that same posture the single-valued field has refused an expanded record since D1 landed, and born-strict dogfood stores save single-valued lookups through the console today, so a console that posts expanded objects only for its multi-valued control would be an inconsistency nothing evidences.
  - **Escalation:** a read-only dogfood item for the seat: on a fresh showcase, save a project with team members through the console record form and read the stored column back. If the console posts expanded objects, the fix is at the producer (objectui), never a lenient alias in this validator (Prime Directive #12). Not blocking this landing: the warn-first default refuses nothing new, and the strict refusal is the one the single value already carries.
- **O4, `assertReferencesResolve`'s "already-expanded objects are skipped" note** now describes a warn-first-only path. Comment accuracy; `engine.ts` was read-only under the claim; a one-line edit for the next PR in this lane that opens `engine.ts`. Agreed, carrier none.
- **The docs-drift advisory on the PR** (five hand-written pages, via the `invalid_option` and `unrecognized_keys` literals): both literals are moved inside the branch, not changed; the only new author-facing text is the `at index N:` prefix inside the existing detail slot. No documented string changes; no docs edit owed.
- **Check-runs on the head at the final read:** 33 runs, 28 success, 3 skipped by path (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 0 failure, and 2 still in progress: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core (6/6)`. The PR touches no governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); this record is the contract-tier review the narrowing owes before the queue. The verdict below stands on the diff and the card; the queue still waits for those two to complete green, and a red on either returns the PR to the dev, not to this record.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22908-multi-reference-element-shape`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Adopted by `domain:engine#2` (`session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`) at 2026-10-12T05:00Z from an isolated at-tier reviewer whose transcript shows read-only tool use (its one write is its own scratch record). The two runs pending at the record's final read have since concluded: on this head `Lint & Repo Gates` and all six `Test Core` shards are `success`; 31 success, 3 skipped, 0 failed. On ②: the seat keeps `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` as triage and the claim declared it. The rule reads "a declaration of `yes` for a narrowing is never an error", and correcting only the PR body would put it out of step with the changeset's own line.

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
